/Issued 409 PM MST Sat Nov 14 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

The upper ridge axis over the CONUS Central Plains will continue
to propagate eastward with strong southerly flow over Montana
transitioning to Southwesterly flow over the next 12 to 24 hours.
With support from a broad negatively tilted trough extending from
the PNW through Western CONUS, a weak upper-level disturbance 
will perturbate through the flow bringing generally light showery
precipitation over Southwest MT through the afternoon hours. Due 
to surface warming and ABL mixing, WBZ heights will stay around 
3000 FT so snow will be contained to the mountain ranges. There is
a stable layer over the Northern regions of the state with weak 
easterly flow keeping low-level fog producing moisture trapped 
along the Milk River Valley until early this afternoon when 
diurnal boundary layer mixing occurs. 

For Sunday, warm and dry conditions will persist with
Southwesterly flow aloft maintaining warm air advection to keep
temperatures in the 50s and 60s. With the approaching Pacific 
trough, pressure gradient winds will increase over Southwest MT 
with gusts up to 40 mph expected within the valley downslope 
regions Sunday morning into the afternoon. 

Beginning Monday night, the Pacific system will kick a strong 
upper-level shortwave trough out over western CONUS bringing deep
ascending moisture and instability over Montana into Wednesday and
fueling cyclogenesis over the Yellowstone area. This low pressure
system will deepen and move eastward across the Continental Divide
pulling colder Canadian air south into the region and creating
widespread snow across the CWA by Tuesday night. Moisture laden 
Southwesterly flow aloft with cold northerly advection will 
provide healthy snow growth zone profiles over much of the state.
Most likely placement for a weak deformation zone to develop will
be Northwest of the low over Western and Central MT. - Akins

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Strong Winds in the Madison River Valley Sunday...

NBM5.2 probabilistic data suggests a 10-30% chance that sustained winds
from the southern end of the Madison River Valley to Norris Hill 
could exceed 40 mph from the late morning hours through early 
evening hours on Sunday, with a 5-10% chance that gusts could 
exceed 55 mph over this same timeframe. BUFKIT soundings and 
deterministic guidance support southwesterly wind speeds of 
20-30kts through H700 over this timeframe, with a weak-to-moderate
surface pressure gradient orientated from west to east along the 
I-90 corridor from Cardwell to Livingston. While these wind speeds
and the overall strength of the gradient are not high enough to 
warrant a High Wind Warning there is a low end chance that during 
peak mixing on Sunday that sustained winds within the Madison 
River Valley could approach high wind criteria (i.e. 40 mph for 1+
hours). - Moldan

Precipitation this Work Week...

For the upcoming winter event Tuesday, ensembles are 
signaling a potential weak deformation zone for moderate snowfall
setting up approximately over Helena and Great Falls. ECMWF and 
GFS show similar mesoscale band placement within the broader 
pattern however intensity, exact location, and duration still 
diverge. Most snowfall estimates for lower elevation areas are 1-4
inches over the Monday night to Wednesday timeframe. Next run 
will bring event time within most short-medium range ensemble 
members for higher fidelity scenario creation. 

The table below lists the reasonable low end (25th Percentile),
most likely (50th Percentile), and high end (75th Percentile) QPF
(liquid equivalent) and snowfall amounts within the NBM5.2 for

Friday. The low end scenario has a 75% chance that amounts will 
exceed the listed value or a 25% chance that amounts will be lower
than what is listed while the high end scenario has a 75% chance 
that amounts will be lower than what is listed or a 25% chance 
that amounts will be higher than what is listed.
